# Tobit Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** In-that day Tobit was-reminded of the money which he-had-deposited with Gabael in-Rages of-Media,

**4:2** and he-said in his-heart, "I have-requested death; why do-I-not call Tobias my-son, so-that I-may-make-known to-him [concerning] this money before I-die?"

**4:3** And he-called him and said, "Child, if I-die, bury me, and do-not despise your-mother; honor her all-the days of-your-life, and do [what is] pleasing to-her, and do-not grieve her.

**4:4** Remember her, child, that-many dangers she-saw for your-sake in her womb. When she-dies, bury her beside me in-the same grave.

**4:5** All-the days, child, remember the-Lord our-God, and do-not wish to-sin and to-transgress his commandments. Do-righteousness all-the days of-your-life, and do-not walk in-the ways of-unrighteousness.

**4:6** For if you-do the-truth, there-will-be success in your-deeds; and to-all those-doing righteousness.

**4:7** From your-possessions do eleēmosynē, and do-not let your-eye be-grudging when you-do eleēmosynē. Do-not turn your-face from any-one of-the poor, and the-face of-God will-not be-turned away from you.

**4:8** As-much-as you-have, in-proportion do eleēmosynē from it; if little you-have, according-to the little do-not be-afraid to-give eleēmosynē.

**4:9** For a-good store you-are-laying-up for yourself for a-day of-necessity.

**4:10** For eleēmosynē from death rescues and does-not allow [a-man] to-enter into-the darkness.

**4:11** A-great confidence before the-Most-High is eleēmosynē for all-those giving it.

**4:12** Beware, child, of-all fornication, and first take to-yourself a-wife from the-seed of-your-fathers, and do-not take a-foreign wife, one-not from the-tribe of-your-father; for we are sons of-the prophets. Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob our-fathers from-of-old — remember, child, that all of-them took wives from their-brethren, and they-were-blessed in their-children, and their-seed will-inherit the-land.

**4:13** And now, child, love your-brethren, and do-not act-arrogantly in your-heart against your-brethren and the-sons and daughters of-your-people, taking a-wife for-yourself from among them; for in-arrogance there-is ruin and great disorder, and in-idleness there-is poverty and deficiency; for idleness is-the mother of-famine.

**4:14** The-wage of-every man who-labors-for-you do-not let it remain with-you until-morning, but give it to-him forthwith; and if you-serve God, it-will-be repaid to-you. Take-heed to-yourself, child, in all your-deeds, and be-disciplined in all your-conduct.

**4:15** What you-hate, do-not do to-any-one. Wine to-excess do-not drink, and drunkenness let-not accompany you on your-way.

**4:16** From your-bread give to-the hungry, and from your-garments [give] to-the naked. From all your-surplus do eleēmosynē, and let-not your-eye grudge when you-do eleēmosynē.

**4:17** Pour out your-bread upon the-grave of-the righteous, and do-not give to-sinners.

**4:18** Seek-counsel from every wise-man, and do-not despise any-profitable advice.

**4:19** In every season bless the-Lord God, and ask from him that your-ways may-be-made-straight and all your-paths and counsels may-prosper; for not every nation has-counsel, but the-Lord himself gives every good thing, and he-humbles whomever he-wills, according-as he-wills. And now, child, remember my-commandments, and let-them not be-blotted-out from your-heart.

**4:20** And now I-make-known to-you the-ten-talents of-silver which I-deposited with Gabael son-of Gabrias at Rages of-Media.

**4:21** And do-not fear, child, that we-have-become poor; you-have many things if you-fear God and flee from every sin and do what-is-good before the-Lord your-God.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

- **4:7, 4:8, 4:10, 4:11, 4:16**: eleēmosynē (ἐλεημοσύνη) preserved untranslated throughout; this term encompasses almsgiving, acts of mercy, and covenant faithfulness — no single English word captures it. Gloss: [merciful-charity].
- **4:12**: "seed of your fathers" is literal; the biological/genealogical sense is primary. The list Noah–Abraham–Isaac–Jacob follows Sinaiticus; some MSS vary the patriarchal list.
- **4:15**: The negative Golden Rule. Greek: *ho miseis, mēdeni poiēsēs* — exact word-for-word: "what you-hate, to-no-one do." This is among the earliest attested forms of the principle.
- **4:17**: "Pour out your bread upon the grave" — Greek *ekcheai* (pour/spread). The practice of funeral meals for the righteous is reflected here; see also Sir 7:33.
- **4:20**: "ten talents of silver" — Sinaiticus reads *deka talanta* here; GI (shorter recension) differs. Retained as-is.
- **4:6**: Greek conditional structure preserved: *ean poiēs tēn alētheian* — "if you do the truth" rather than idiomatic "if you act truthfully." — EMET
